newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-HUGHES AND GULLIT PUT THE ICING ON CHELSEA'S CAK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-HUGHES AND GULLIT PUT THE ICING ON CHELSEA'S CAK.

text.p: Chelsea fans had three great reasons to celebrate on Monday.

The first was their comprehensive 3-0 victory over Wimbledon in a one-sided English Football Association (F.A.) Cup semifinal at Highbury on Sunday which put them in the cup final for the second time in four seasons.
The second was Dutch coach Ruud Gullit's denial of a newspaper report that he was considering leaving Chelsea to return to the Netherlands.
And the third was the news that Welsh striker Mark Hughes was set to stay with the club for at least another two years.
For Chelsea fans already delirious with joy, Hughes's announcement put the icing on the cake after a memorable day for the London side.

Hughes not only scored twice -- his second goal of the game, lashed home from an acute angle in the last minute, giving the game its emphatic scoreline -- but afterwards confirmed that his immediate future would be spent wearing Chelsea blue.
The 33-year-old Hughes, who will join an elite band of players when he appears in his fifth cup final next month, said he was delighted to be staying with Chelsea.

After the match Gullit said that Hughes had already accepted a year-long extension to his current contract which would keep him at Stamford Bridge until 1999 but Hughes said that was not strictly true.
"I have got to discuss it with my wife," said the Welshman. "She's the one that makes all the decisions -- as well as spending all my money!
"But I don't think there's going to be a problem. At my age anybody would want a longer deal but I am reasonably pleased with the offer and I don't think I did my case any harm today."
Hughes was indeed inspirational in the way he kept battling against a resolute Wimbledon backline, getting his reward with the opening goal after 42 minutes.
Gianfranco Zola put the game beyond Wimbledon's reach with a superbly-taken second goal after 64 minutes, before Hughes scored the 26th F.A. Cup goal of his career in the dying seconds.

Barring injury Hughes will join an elite of 10 men who have made five cup final appearances this century -- and will become the first this century to earn four winners' medals if Chelsea win the cup against either Chesterfield or Middlesbrough on May 17.
Hughes admitted there was some doubt about the longevity of his career at the highest level when he left Manchester United for Chelsea two years ago.
"When I came here there were a few raised eyebrows but I knew which way this club wanted to move and I haven't been disappointed."
Gullit also pledged his future to Chelsea when he denied a report that he wanted to leave London to return to Feyenoord.
"That's not right," he said, "Everyone knows Feyenoord is my club in Holland and is very close to my heart but that is for the future. Any move at the moment is not negotiable.

"I will stay at Chelsea for a couple more years at least. I am very happy and grateful that Chelsea have given me this chance so early in my career and I have a lot of work to do here. I have no intention of leaving now."

Gullit will make history by becoming the first overseas coach to lead out a team in the final, while Hughes is having such a fine season that he could yet end it by being named as Footballer of the Year.
No Chelsea player has won that honour since it was first awarded to Sir Stanley Matthews in 1948.
